headline: Sow one more round of fall crops now — the window for direct-sown greens and roots closes over the next 2–3 weeks.

tasks.title: Direct-sow fall greens & roots
tasks.detail: Lettuce, spinach, arugula, kale, chard, plus beets, carrots, and turnips. With first frost around mid-October, these have time if sown in the next couple of weeks. Keep the seedbed damp in the August heat until they’re up.

tasks.title: Pick often to keep plants producing
tasks.detail: Harvest zucchini and cucumbers every day or two, snap beans while slender, and pull the first ripe tomatoes. Frequent picking keeps beans and squash setting new fruit.

tasks.title: Deep, consistent watering
tasks.detail: An inch-plus per week, early morning at the base. Even moisture now prevents blossom-end rot on tomatoes and bitterness or splitting in cukes and greens.

tasks.title: Scout for late-summer pests & blight
tasks.detail: Check for squash bugs, tomato hornworms, and cucumber beetles and hand-pick them. Watch tomatoes and potatoes for early/late blight in humid spells — remove affected leaves and open up airflow.

tasks.title: Side-dress the heavy feeders
tasks.detail: A light feeding for tomatoes, peppers, and winter squash to carry them through the final push. Go easy on nitrogen so you get fruit, not just leaves.

tasks.title: Look ahead to succession & garlic
tasks.detail: As peas and early beans finish, clear the beds and sow a quick round of greens or a cover crop. Order seed garlic now for planting in October.
